narrative: Material PL1__MAAD5FC2 exhibits a smooth demand regime (CV=0.376) with a mean daily working-day demand of ~657 units and no statistically detectable trend across the observed period (March 2025–March 2026). Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.901) driven predominantly by transport variability, which accounts for 82% of lead-time demand variance and necessitates a safety stock increase from 540 to 868 units to sustain a 95% service level. An (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 2,801 units (above the 1,751 MOQ) is recommended; this is comfortably within the 8,404-unit storage capacity at 43.7% utilisation. The most impactful lever for further cost reduction is reducing lead time variability through supplier/logistics collaboration.
warnings: Lead time CV=0.901 is highly unstable; two extreme observations (4.05, 3.15 WD) inflate safety stock requirement significantly.
SAP safety lead time of 3.0 days exceeds the analytically recommended 1.32 days — consider reducing to release working capital.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous and smooth (CV=0.376, non-zero fraction=1.0) with no intermittency, making a fixed-order-quantity EOQ model appropriate. The high lead time variability justifies a continuous-review trigger (reorder point) rather than a periodic review. MOQ=1,751 is below EOQ=2,801, so EOQ governs and MOQ is non-binding.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Capacity utilisation post-replenishment is 43.7% (3,669 / 8,404 units). No capacity constraint binds under the recommended policy. However, if mean demand rises by >25% or safety stock is increased further, the capacity ceiling should be re-evaluated.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Lead time instability (CV=0.90) is the primary service risk. Two outlier deliveries (4.05 and 3.15 WD) inflated the safety stock requirement by an estimated 30%. Escalation to procurement/logistics recommended to investigate and reduce lead time variance.
